title: Maine Air National Guard Fuel Cell Hangar (FCH), Project No. FKNN159044
description: UPDATE: The solicitation has not been cleared for release. The tentative dates below have shifted. Invitation for Bids (IFB) Unrestricted / Full and Open NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction The Maine Air National Guard intends to issue an Invitation for Bids (IFB) to award a single firm-fixed-price contract for non-personal services to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a new 42,374 square foot Fuel Cell Hangar facility at Bangor Air National Guard Base, Bangor, Maine, in accordance with the drawings and specifications for Project No. FKNN159044. The contract duration will be 670 calendar days after notice to proceed, to include inspection and punch list. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this work is 236220. The small business size standard is $45,000,000. This action is being procured on an unrestricted basis. The magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is on-or-about 20 November 2026. The tentative date for the pre-bid conference is on-or-about 2 December 2026, 1000Hrs local time, location to be provided in the solicitation. Interested contractors are encouraged to attend and shall follow conference registration and base access requirements shown in the solicitation. A site visit will follow the pre-bid conference. All questions for the pre-bid conference must be submitted by 28 October 2026 via email to 101.msg.msc.contracting@us.af.mil. The bid opening date is tentatively planned for on-or-about 6 November 2026. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. Interested offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). To register go to SAM.gov. Instructions for registering are on the website (there is no fee for registration). The solicitation and associated information will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. A Small Business Subcontracting Plan will be required if the bidder is a large business, as set forth in the solicitation. The HUBZone price evaluation preference described at RFO FAR 19.110 will apply. In accordance with RFO FAR 36.101-4, the following information is provided: There are no agency-specific policies or procedures that apply to the definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. No data is available regarding the timely definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1(c), brand name justifications will be included with the solicitation for certain components that must be compatible with existing installation systems, including Sargent Manufacturing Company locks, Monaco Fire Alarm Systems digital addressable fire alarm systems, Honeywell Building/Tridium Niagara-AX direct digital controls, Armstrong World Industries, Inc. acoustical ceiling tiles, Ultima High-NRC Square Lay-in, and Sherwin Williams or approved equal paint. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line item: additive bid item for satellite parking. DISCLAIMER: The official plans and specifications are located on the official government webpage and the Government is not liable for information furnished by any other source. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to Contract Opportunities for electronic downloading. This will normally be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the offeror�s responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. Websites are occasionally inaccessible for various reasons. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for an offeror�s inability to access the documents posted on the referenced web pages. The Government will not issue paper copies.

title: Market Survey for Janitorial Services at FAA Facilities in King Salmon, Alaska
description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting a Market Survey seeking to identify interested and capable sources. Sources must respond with information to confirm evidence of their qualifications and capabilities. Responses to this market Survey will be sued to determine if there is adequate competition to set the requirements aside for Socially and Economically Disadvantage Businesses, small Businesses, or full and open competition. This survey is being conducted in accordance with the FAA Acquisition management System (AMS) Section 3.2.1.2.1. This Market Survey will support market research obtained from multiple sources and will be utilized for planning purposes only. All interested vendors are advised that the FAA will not pay for any information or any administrative costs incurred that are associated with any response received from industry in response to this Market Survey. Therefore, any costs associated with the vendor�s market Survey submissions will be solely at the expense for the interested vendor. The general scope of work under the proposed contract will be that the contractor must provide all labor, supplies, supervision, tools, materials, equipment, transportation, and licenses or permits necessary to provide the janitorial services in accordance with this specification. Janitorial services apply to all designated spaces in support of the ATCT and associated buildings in King Salmon, Alaska. The intended NAICS is 561720, Janitorial Services. Location: King Salmon, Alaska RESPONSE TO THIS MARKET SURVEY: Any information provided in response to this Market Survey will be used for informational purposes only and will not be released. Any proprietary information submitted will be protected if appropriately marked. Vendor participation in any informational session is not a promise of future business with the FAA. Responses must include the following information: Name of the company, including any DBA name Address Phone Point of Contact Email address Business size status; 8(a), Small, SDVOSB, WOSB, etc. Verification of active registration at SAM.gov Submit response for the Market Survey by 4:00 PM., Pacific Time on November 30, 2026, 4:00 PM Pacific Time. Responses including attachments, must be submitted electronically and received in the email inbox of: Angela.Furukawa@faa.gov, by the due date and time stated above. There are no attachments. Note: the scope of work is subject to change prior to the solicitation date.

title: Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Worldwide Expeditionary Multiple Award Contract (WEXMAC) 2.2 Territorial Integrity of the United States (TITUS)
description: Awarded modification to increase their base period contract ceiling with the amount of $45,000,000,000 to support worldwide expeditionary multiple award contract (WEXMAC) territorial integrity of the U.S. (TITUS geographic region). WEXMAC TITUS will provide supplies and services in support of but not limited to supporting the six phases of the continuum of military operations in support of the geographic Combatant Command's joint operations, coalition partners, and other federal agencies in setting and sustaining the theater through the following requirements: theater opening (includes reception, staging, onward-movement, and integration support; sustainment; theater distribution; and stability operations and Defense Support of Civil Authorities support. The WEXMAC TITUS description of contractual scope provides that services and supplies provided through the performance of this contract include but are not limited to humanitarian assistance/disaster relief, contingency, exercise, lodging, logistics, water-based, and land-based support. The base period began in January 2025 and is expected to be completed by December 2029; if all options are exercised, the performance period will be completed by December 2034. The increased contract ceiling modifications will be incorporated into the contractors' existing base performance period with one five-year option with individual requirements performed under task orders when specific dates and locations are identified. If the option period is exercised, the total estimated contract maximum for each contractor could be $65,000,000,000.

title: PILOT PROGRAM TO ASSIST CERTAIN MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND DEPENDENTS WITH ADDITIONAL SUPPLEMENTAL COVERAGE RELATING TO CANCER HT9402-26-RFI-0255
description: UPDATE: 11/06/2026 The Government received noteworthy interest in one-on-one meetings. The attachment labeled �Supplemental Cancer Insurance Pilot_Industry Event� contains crucial information for Vendor presentations. The Defense Health Agency continues market research with the following primary objectives: Investigate feasibility of no-cost, fixed indemnity supplemental cancer insurance for pilot eligible TRICARE beneficiaries based on industry interest and capability to meet requirements. Reduce financial burden and support beneficiary wellness, family resilience, and force readiness in the event of cancer diagnosis. Appraise potential value added to beneficiaries to inform pilot implementation and future policy regarding supplemental benefits. Virtual meetings will last approximately 1hr and are available on the following dates/times: 17NOV2026 @1000 EST 17NOV2026@ 1300 EST 17NOV2026@ 1500 EST 19NOV2026@ 1400 EST [alternate] Presentation materials will be due one business day before the event (16NOV). Please email Mr. James Goddard to reserve a one-on-one meeting. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- UPDATE: 10/21/2026 The Government received several questions in the RFI submissions. The attachment labeled �RFI QA Responses HT940226RFI0255 Supplemental Pilot" is intended to address these questions. The DHA plans to continue gathering market intelligence by meeting with interested vendors. Vendor�s will be expected to address questions regarding their RFI submissions as well as general market intelligence needed by the Government and will be given the opportunity to ask the Government questions. Virtual meetings are anticipated to be held on 19 November 2026. Please email Mr. James Goddard to request a one-on-one meeting. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is currently in the planning phase for partnering with carriers of supplemental insurance focused on cancer coverage. This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to initiate market research efforts as the Government considers structuring processes to meet Congress� intent. Section 734 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 (Enclosure 1) requires DHA to establish a pilot program not later than September 30, 2027, under which members of the regular component of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force and their dependents enrolled in TRICARE may obtain supplemental cancer insurance for noncovered expenses under a fixed indemnity supplemental benefit. The supplemental coverage is intended to provide financial assistance for noncovered expenses related to cancer screening, diagnosis and treatment that are not otherwise covered by the health care benefits the individuals receive under chapter 55 of title 10, United States Code, or any other benefit provided by the Secretary of Defense. https://www.congress.gov/119/plaws/publ60/PLAW-119publ60.pdf RFI Instructions: Prepare and submit a written response addressing each of the questions below. This response shall not exceed 20 pages in length and should not be solely your company�s general capability statement but instead specifically address the Government�s topics listed in this RFI. Please send your responses to the Defense Health Agency, Managed Care Contracting Division james.goddard22.ctr@health.mil by Close of Business 18 September 2026. RFI Questions: Plan Types and Coverage Scope Describe how a TRICARE specific plan would differ from current commercially available plans. What non-covered services under TRICARE would be covered? Would there be portability options if a beneficiary is no longer eligible for TRICARE? How could your company intend to add value to TRICARE beneficiaries? Describe an applicable case scenario. Coverage Details and Exclusions Detail general coverages provided in similar plans. Would there be any key coverage exclusions and limitations, including but not limited to: Acts of War, specific cancer types, pregnancy, and state-based restrictions? What annual or lifetime maximums on benefits would apply, and what conditions or treatments would be subject to caps or exceptions? What coverage would be provided for non-FDA approved drugs, participation in clinical trials, or other emerging and unproven treatments? Would pre-existing conditions be covered? If yes, what conditions would be included? Would there be any coverage limitations for a recurring diagnosis (remission or new)? In which states does your company offer coverage, and are there any state specific exceptions or restrictions that would apply to a TRICARE specific plan? How would this impact our mobile beneficiary population? Do your company�s plans provide coverage for beneficiaries residing or receiving care overseas? Eligibility and Enrollment Per the NDAA, the Government will not be subsidizing this pilot. To be financially viable, is there a minimum required enrollment threshold for such an unsubsidized, �no cost,� 100% beneficiary paid, group plan to be offered by your company? Is there a preferred eligibility verification process? What would prevent a member from being eligible? Describe the enrollment process and the expected burden on the beneficiary. When would coverage be effective? Any limitations? How would beneficiaries make premium payments? How are premiums structured today (in similar policies)? How would your company structure TRICARE premiums based on pilot requirements? Would premium rates be locked in for the duration of the pilot? Describe the termination of coverage process and the expected burden on the beneficiary. Claims and Payments How are claim payments determined and processed, including if lump sum payments are one-time or recurring, and any applicable limitations? Would payments be taxable as income? How would beneficiaries submit claims/receive payments, and what is the expected burden on the beneficiary? Would there be any third-party liability? If so, please explain. Describe the claims submissions and processing experience, including the average processing time and the availability of digital tools (such as online portals or mobile apps) for beneficiaries to submit and track claims. Reporting and Oversight What beneficiary data would your company provide to the Government/employer (e.g. cost, number of enrollees, denials, customer satisfaction, use case data)? Are there any limitations to data your company would be willing to share? Does your company recommend any specific data metrics DHA should track to accurately report the program�s success, beneficiary satisfaction, and programmatic feasibility to Congress? What board or organization oversees the supplemental insurance industry? Give some examples of standards, grievances, or reporting at a state or federal level. Qualifications How many years of experience does your company have providing supplemental insurance plans? What is your company�s claims acceptance/denial rate? What are the top 10 reasons for denials? How will your company protect beneficiaries� personally identifiable information? Acquisition Strategy What are ways to participate via �no-cost� or similar means? Does your company anticipate any barriers to participating in the pilot based on �no-cost� contract terms? title: Maine Air National Guard Fuel Cell Hangar (FCH), Project No. FKNN159044
description: Invitation for Bids (IFB) Unrestricted / Full and Open NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction The Maine Air National Guard intends to issue an Invitation for Bids (IFB) to award a single firm-fixed-price contract for non-personal services to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a new 42,374 square foot Fuel Cell Hangar facility at Bangor Air National Guard Base, Bangor, Maine, in accordance with the drawings and specifications for Project No. FKNN159044. The contract duration will be 670 calendar days after notice to proceed, to include inspection and punch list. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this work is 236220. The small business size standard is $45,000,000. This action is being procured on an unrestricted basis. The magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is on-or-about 6 October 2026. The tentative date for the pre-bid conference is on-or-about 21 October 2026, 1000Hrs local time, location to be provided in the solicitation. Interested contractors are encouraged to attend and shall follow conference registration and base access requirements shown in the solicitation. A site visit will follow the pre-bid conference. All questions for the pre-bid conference must be submitted by 28 October 2026 via email to 101.msg.msc.contracting@us.af.mil. The bid opening date is tentatively planned for on-or-about 6 November 2026. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. Interested offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). To register go to SAM.gov. Instructions for registering are on the website (there is no fee for registration). The solicitation and associated information will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. A Small Business Subcontracting Plan will be required if the bidder is a large business, as set forth in the solicitation. The HUBZone price evaluation preference described at RFO FAR 19.110 will apply. In accordance with RFO FAR 36.101-4, the following information is provided: There are no agency-specific policies or procedures that apply to the definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. No data is available regarding the timely definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1(c), brand name justifications will be included with the solicitation for certain components that must be compatible with existing installation systems, including Sargent Manufacturing Company locks, Monaco Fire Alarm Systems digital addressable fire alarm systems, Honeywell Building/Tridium Niagara-AX direct digital controls, Armstrong World Industries, Inc. acoustical ceiling tiles, Ultima High-NRC Square Lay-in, and Sherwin Williams or approved equal paint. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line item: additive bid item for satellite parking. title: RRC Services located within the city limits of the following cities within San Bernardino County, CA: San Bernardino, Fontana, Rancho Cucamonga, Bloomington, Colton, Grand Terrace, Highland, Loma Linda, and Redlands
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (Bureau) is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes located within the city limits of the following cities within San Bernardino County, CA: San Bernardino, Fontana, Rancho Cucamonga, Bloomington, Colton, Grand Terrace, Highland, Loma Linda, and Redlands and Home Confinement radius is within 100 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work entitled, "Residential Reentry Center, March 2022 SOW�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, Programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity type contract with firm fixed unit prices for all line items. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a maximum of 70 beds in which 56 beds will be designated for males and 14 beds designated for females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a maximum of 40 placements to include both males and females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods. The Home Confinement Radius must be within 100 miles of the RRC facility. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The DHA plans to continue gathering market intelligence by meeting with interested vendors. Vendor�s will be expected to address questions regarding their RFI submissions as well as general market intelligence needed by the Government and will be given the opportunity to ask the Government questions. Virtual meetings are anticipated to be held on 19 November 2026. Please email Mr. James Goddard to request a one-on-one meeting. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is currently in the planning phase for partnering with carriers of supplemental insurance focused on cancer coverage. This Request for Information (RFI) is intended to initiate market research efforts as the Government considers structuring processes to meet Congress� intent. Section 734 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 (Enclosure 1) requires DHA to establish a pilot program not later than September 30, 2027, under which members of the regular component of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force and their dependents enrolled in TRICARE may obtain supplemental cancer insurance for noncovered expenses under a fixed indemnity supplemental benefit. The supplemental coverage is intended to provide financial assistance for noncovered expenses related to cancer screening, diagnosis and treatment that are not otherwise covered by the health care benefits the individuals receive under chapter 55 of title 10, United States Code, or any other benefit provided by the Secretary of Defense. https://www.congress.gov/119/plaws/publ60/PLAW-119publ60.pdf RFI Instructions: Prepare and submit a written response addressing each of the questions below. This response shall not exceed 20 pages in length and should not be solely your company�s general capability statement but instead specifically address the Government�s topics listed in this RFI. Please send your responses to the Defense Health Agency, Managed Care Contracting Division james.goddard22.ctr@health.mil by Close of Business 18 September 2026. RFI Questions: Plan Types and Coverage Scope Describe how a TRICARE specific plan would differ from current commercially available plans. What non-covered services under TRICARE would be covered? Would there be portability options if a beneficiary is no longer eligible for TRICARE? How could your company intend to add value to TRICARE beneficiaries? Describe an applicable case scenario. Coverage Details and Exclusions Detail general coverages provided in similar plans. Would there be any key coverage exclusions and limitations, including but not limited to: Acts of War, specific cancer types, pregnancy, and state-based restrictions? What annual or lifetime maximums on benefits would apply, and what conditions or treatments would be subject to caps or exceptions? What coverage would be provided for non-FDA approved drugs, participation in clinical trials, or other emerging and unproven treatments? Would pre-existing conditions be covered? If yes, what conditions would be included? Would there be any coverage limitations for a recurring diagnosis (remission or new)? In which states does your company offer coverage, and are there any state specific exceptions or restrictions that would apply to a TRICARE specific plan? How would this impact our mobile beneficiary population? Do your company�s plans provide coverage for beneficiaries residing or receiving care overseas? Eligibility and Enrollment Per the NDAA, the Government will not be subsidizing this pilot. To be financially viable, is there a minimum required enrollment threshold for such an unsubsidized, �no cost,� 100% beneficiary paid, group plan to be offered by your company? Is there a preferred eligibility verification process? What would prevent a member from being eligible? Describe the enrollment process and the expected burden on the beneficiary. When would coverage be effective? Any limitations? How would beneficiaries make premium payments? How are premiums structured today (in similar policies)? How would your company structure TRICARE premiums based on pilot requirements? Would premium rates be locked in for the duration of the pilot? Describe the termination of coverage process and the expected burden on the beneficiary. Claims and Payments How are claim payments determined and processed, including if lump sum payments are one-time or recurring, and any applicable limitations? Would payments be taxable as income? How would beneficiaries submit claims/receive payments, and what is the expected burden on the beneficiary? Would there be any third-party liability? If so, please explain. Describe the claims submissions and processing experience, including the average processing time and the availability of digital tools (such as online portals or mobile apps) for beneficiaries to submit and track claims. Reporting and Oversight What beneficiary data would your company provide to the Government/employer (e.g. cost, number of enrollees, denials, customer satisfaction, use case data)? Are there any limitations to data your company would be willing to share? Does your company recommend any specific data metrics DHA should track to accurately report the program�s success, beneficiary satisfaction, and programmatic feasibility to Congress? What board or organization oversees the supplemental insurance industry? Give some examples of standards, grievances, or reporting at a state or federal level. Qualifications How many years of experience does your company have providing supplemental insurance plans? What is your company�s claims acceptance/denial rate? What are the top 10 reasons for denials? How will your company protect beneficiaries� personally identifiable information? Acquisition Strategy What are ways to participate via �no-cost� or similar means? Does your company anticipate any barriers to participating in the pilot based on �no-cost� contract terms? title: CO BR UCPO Blue Mesa Road(1) Blue Mesa Road
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR BID � PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS ARE NOT AVAILABLE. PROJECT NAME: CO BR UCPO Blue Mesa Road(1) Blue Mesa Road Blue Mesa Road is a 1.44-mile corridor located in Gunnison County, CO and provides access to the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR) Power Plant and Pine Creek Trailhead recreational activities on the Curecanti National Recreational Area. SCOPE OF THE WORK Schedule A: Proposed rehabilitation of 0.86 miles to replace existing gravel roadway with asphalt concrete pavement. Reconstruction/Rehabilitation, as needed, for 0.24 miles of existing asphalt to incorporate raising roadway profile at US 50 intersection, drainage improvements including replacement and/or lining of damaged culverts, relocation of traffic counters, formalize parking area with ADA stalls, signing and striping, ditch reconditioning, rockfall mitigation. Option X: Proposed rehabilitation of 0.34 miles to replace existing gravel roadway with asphalt concrete pavement from BOR gate to Blue Mesa Power Plant, drainage improvements to include replacement of damaged culverts, signing and striping, ditch reconditioning, installation of 6� electrical conduit for purposes of future automatic gate installation. Option Y: Proposed 6-inch electric conduit installation and 2 ft x 2 ft max trenching for 2,215 LF miles from the electric security gate to The Blue Mesa Power Plant. Conduit will provide future access for BOR to provide electric connection to security gate. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: Schedule A: 15225-0000 Slope, Reference, and Clearing and Grubbing Control: 1.051 MILE 20301-1900 Removal of Pipe Culvert: 5 EACH 20401-0000 Roadway Excavation: 1,500 CU YD 30201-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 2,500 CU YD 30302-1000 Ditch Reconditioning: 3,280 LN FT 40301-0100 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Type 1: 2,500 TON 60103-0140 Concrete, Headwall for 24-Inch Pipe Culvert (L-Shaped): 3 EACH 60103-0160 Concrete, Headwall for 30-Inch Pipe Culvert: 1 EACH 60103-0280 Concrete, Headwall for 66-Inch Pipe Culvert (Includes Wingwalls): 1 EACH 60201-0800 24-Inch Pipe Culvert: 255 LN FT 60201-0900 30-Inch Pipe Culvert: 45 LN FT 60707-1200 Lining 66-Inch Pipe Culvert (HDPE Slipline): 110 LN FT 60707-1300 Lining 72-Inch Pipe Culvert (HDPE Slipline): 190 LN FT 63401-0300 Pavement Markings, Type B, Solid: 46,000 LN FT Option X: 15225-0000 Slope, Reference, and Clearing and Grubbing Control: 0.38 MILE 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 200 CU YD 30201-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 700 CU YD 40301-0100 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Type 1: 650 TON 56603-0000 Reinforced Shotcrete: 180 SQ YD 60704-0000 Cleaning Culvert in Place: 7 EA 63401-0300 Pavement Markings, Type B, Solid: 8,500 LN FT Option Y: 63610-3410 Conduit, 6-Inch, HDPE (Schedule 40): 2,215 LN FT 63621-1000 Utility Box, Pullbox: 6 EA 63622-0000 Utility Trench: 2,215 LN FT ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE Advertisement: November 2026 Award: January 2027 NTP: April 2027 Construction: May 2027- October 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Between $2,000,000 and $5,000,000 A NON-MANDATORY PRE-BID SITE VISIT WILL BE HELD NOVEMBER 4TH, 2026 AT 10:00AM. title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF -Ermittlung und Bewertung von Dieselmotoremissionen (DME) von Fahrzeugen der Fremdrettungskräfte in Eisenbahntunneln
description: Bei Eisenbahntunneln gemäß der EBA-Ril-Tunnel (Zwei-Röhrenprinzip) ist es im Ereignisfall (z.B. Brand) vorgesehen, dass Einsatzfahrzeuge der Fremdrettungskräfte in die andere, nicht vom Ereignis betroffene Röhre einfahren. Die Fahrzeuge verfügen nahezu ausschließlich über einen Antrieb per Dieselmotor, welcher bei Betrieb entsprechende Emissionen verursacht (Abgase). Im Gegensatz zu Straßentunneln sind in elektrifizierten Eisenbahntunneln keine Systeme zur Abgasabführung vorgesehen. Im Rahmen von Planfeststellungsvorhaben (Beteiligung als Träger öffentlicher Belange) kommt es daher seitens der Fremdrettungskräfte zu Einwänden, dass ein dauerhafter Betrieb von Diesel-Einsatzfahrzeugen im Tunnel auf Grund der Dieselmotoremissionen (DME) nicht möglich sei und die Abgase einen Aufenthalt von Einsatzkräften in der Tunnelröhre auf Dauer verhindern. Gleichwohl bestehen in Bahntunneln üblicherweise natürliche Luftströme, die entsprechende Abgase abführen könnten. Es fehlen derzeit auch Ergebnisse/Erkenntnisse im Allgemeinen zu Strömungsgeschwindigkeiten und deren Auswirkungen auf Luftschadstoffbelastungen in Tunneln in Abhängigkeiten verschiedener Geometrien von Eisenbahntunneln.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Ausgleich volatiler Energieerzeugung im Bahnstromnetz
description: Mit dem Bundes-Klimaschutzgesetz (KSG), das die Erfüllung der nationalen Klimaschutzziele gewährleisten soll und mit dem Klimaschutzplan 20250 festgelegte Klimaschutz- und Sektorziele gesetzlich verankert hat, soll in Deutschland bis zum Jahr 2045 die Treibhausgasneutralität erreicht werden. Derzeit wird der Bahnstrom aus einem gemischten Portfolio aus eigenen konventionellen Kraftwerken, Erneuerbare-Energien-Anlagen, sowie den Bezug aus dem öffentlichen Stromnetz bereitgestellt. Die Strategie zur Erhöhung des Anteils an Erneuerbaren Energien (EE) basiert u.a. auf den Abschluss von Grünstrom-Lieferverträgen auf nationaler als auch europäischer Ebene sowie den Zubau von EE-Erzeugungsanlagen auf Bahnbetriebsanlagen. Dabei wird seit April 2023 erstmals Strom direkt in das deutsche Bahnstromnetz eingespeist. Weiterhin wird durch die aktuelle Gesetzgebung die Erhöhung des Anteils von EE-Anlagen durch das Allgemeine Eisenbahn-Gesetz (AEG) §18f bzw. dem Gesetz zum Ausbau erneuerbarer Energien (EEG) §37 vorangetrieben. Der Anteil regenerativ bereitgestelltem Strom am Bahnstrommix lag im Jahr 2025 bereits bei 71,5 %. Der zunehmende Ausbau bzw. fluktuierende EE-Einspeiseanlagen wie Photovoltaik und Windkraftanlagen mit einer inhärent schwankenden Energiebereitstellung, sowie die prognostizierte Zunahme im Schienenverkehr erhöhen die Komplexität einer sicheren und nachhaltigen Energieversorgung. Hohe Lastgradienten auf Erzeuger- als auch Verbraucherseite und der Wegfall bisheriger konventioneller Kraftwerkstechnik zur Gewährleistung der Netzstabilität im Bahnstromnetz, bringen neue technische und wirtschaftliche Fragestellungen mit sich. Insbesondere die zunehmende Erhöhung leistungselektronischer Komponenten und dessen Wechselwirkung im Gesamtsystem Schiene erhöhen die Komplexität im Bahnstromnetz. Ziel des Projektes ist es, die Auswirkungen des steigenden EE-Anteils auf das Bahnstromnetz respektive auf das öffentliche Landesnetz zu untersuchen und technische und wirtschaftliche Anforderungen bzw. Maßnahmen für Energiespeichersysteme daraus abzuleiten. Das Vorhaben soll eine sichere Energieversorgung im Bahnstromnetz und eine zukünftige bedarfsgerechte Netzplanung unterstützen und den notwendigen Ausbau von EE-Erzeugungsanlagen im Bahnstromnetz stärken, um eine Umsetzung des Klimaschutzplans 2050 für ein treibhausneutrales Verkehrssystem im Jahr 2045 zu gewährleisten.
